text:
mei: Quick heads-up — kestrel-v2 int8 onboarding shows a localized chrF drop on JP->AR samples where punctuation and zero-width joiners mix.
olga: Can you paste a tiny repro and token dumps?
mei: minimal case below. FP16 vs INT8 detok and token lists from the tokenizer harness:
```
Source: 

















FP16 tokens: ["東","\u4eac","\u00b7","\u0627","\u0644","\u0623","\u062e","\u0628","\u0627","\u0631","\u2014","\u30ab","\u30b9","\u200d"]
INT8 tokens: ["東","\u4eac","\u30fb","\u0627","\u0644","\u0623","\u062e","\u0628","\u0627","\u0631","-","\u30ab","\u30b9","\u200c"]
```
(mei: note U+00B7 vs U+30FB, U+2014 vs hyphen, U+200D vs U+200C toggles)
tae: That looks like a tokenizer normalizer mismatch combined with compact-vocab ordering during int8 build. token ids differ before model.
olga: CI smoke: kestrel-v2-int8 4959004470: chrf_base=0.655 chrf_int8=0.611 reg_count=274 top-pattern="mid-dot-zwj-seam"
mei: Proposed mitigation: ingress canonicalizer NFKC + explicit mapping table: map U+00B7->U+30FB, U+2014->U+002D, map U+200D->U+200C (but emit metric for replacements). Add unit fixtures tests/locale/mid_dot_zwj_cases.txt and assert token stability post-canonicalization.
tae: Put behind feature flag tokenize.canonicalize_unicode and canary 3% int8 traffic. If that recovers >90% regressions, we merge and roll. Otherwise escalate to tokenizer artifact serialization audit.
ci-bot: canary-plan kestrel-int8-canon 4959004488: route 3% int8 traffic; collect BLEU/chrF + token-dumps.
mei: assigning owners: mei normalizer PR, tae tests + canary, olga metrics. Will update when canary runs. :thumbsup:
